children: SYDNEY--Australian house prices posted a sixth straight monthly fall in September, with economists expecting the retreat to extend well into next year as interest rates continue to rise.
National dwelling values fell 1.1% in September, taking the cumulative decline since a peak in March to 5.2% nationally, property research group Cotality said Wednesday.
Every capital city except Darwin recorded a fall in home values through the first month of spring, the data showed.
The drop in house prices comes as the Reserve Bank of Australia raised interest rates to a 15-year high on Tuesday.

The RBA cited deep concerns about the impact of the unresolved war in the Middle East, a boom in investment in the artificial intelligence sector, and solid demand locally as triggers for the rise in interest rates.
Economists expects the RBA will raise interest rates further in November, with some forecasting that the tightening cycle will extend into 2027.

Australia's housing downturn reflects a combination of affordability constraints, higher interest rates, elevated living costs, and weaker consumer sentiment, all of which have reduced purchasing capacity and dampened buyer demand, Cotality said.
Brisbane recorded the sharpest monthly decline among the capitals in September, with values down 1.5%, edging past Sydney's 1.4% fall, the data showed.
Sydney continues to lead the housing correction, with values now 8.6% below their February peak, while Melbourne values are 7.2% below their cyclical high in November last year.
Housing turnover has also eased, with estimates of the number of home sales over the past three months 19.1% lower than a year ago nationally and 13.3% below the previous five-year average.

"The sharp drop in sales has implications for the broader economy, with lower sales likely to hit some retail segments as well as tax revenues for state governments," said Tim Lawless, head of research at Cotality.
